intent: Independently audit participation-stage policy03's evidence-authority change against G01 and the complete mode02 diagnostic.
changed_factor: Only the evidence-authority paragraph is replaced. It distinguishes actual learner conduct in conversation from descriptive teaching-material labels and states that a topic preference alone does not establish deliberate refusal. All ordered eligibility/recovery rules, output schema and remaining text match policy02. These two general clarifications are bundled; any measured improvement cannot be attributed to just one.

requirement_review.finding: An exercise title or inventory label describes the material, not the learner's intent. Using actual contributions and conversation turns to establish conduct follows G01 and prevents unsupported intent attribution.

The unchanged ordered rules still use actual history and known Guard state. Warnings can establish context for knowing repetition; a warning alone cannot invent prior Guard or persistent evasion. The new paragraph does not remove those state rules.

A topic preference alone remains distinct from clear deliberate refusal. The preserved obstruction and knowing-rejection branches still permit new Guard entry when evidence beyond the preference establishes it.

Task attempts, substantive intended solutions and relevant clarification restore tutoring when they replace obstruction, including wrong answers. Bare promises and continued deliberate obstruction retain their existing boundaries.
The change makes the source of a participation conclusion inspectable and prohibits teaching-material descriptions from being treated as actual student misconduct.
